title: Learning from Noisy Preferences: A Semi-Supervised Learning Approach to Direct Preference Optimization
claim: Binary labels collapse multi-dimensional preferences into conflicting signals that confuse standard training; ours decouples them into refined timestep-aware signals via self-training.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow with two branches: Diffusion DPO (top) vs Semi-DPO (bottom)
description: A wide flow diagram. At top left, a dashed green box shows two generated images of a cow and calf in a grassland (Image A and Image B) next to the text prompt. Below it, a box lists human visual preferences by dimension: composition favors A, semantic alignment favors A, texture favors B. An annotator icon turns this into a single binary label, A > B. From there a red-labeled 'Diffusion DPO' branch goes up to a 'Conflict Signal' box with a red X on texture, then to a confused emoji model and a 'CONFUSED' speech bubble asking what humans like. The green 'Semi-DPO (Ours)' branch goes to a 'Refined Timestep-Aware Signal' panel. This panel has win and lose rows of A/B labels across timesteps from T to 0. It leads to a cycling-arrows 'Training / Pseudo-labeling by itself' loop and a happy party emoji model. Red marks the baseline and green marks ours.
caption: Resolving label noise from multi-dimensional preferences. Standard Diffusion-DPO learns from a noisy, conflict signal created when a binary label (A $\succ$ B) collapses multi-dimensional preferences (e.g., A's composition vs. B's texture). Our method, Semi-DPO, resolves this by decoupling the conflict into refined timestep aware signals via self-training, leading to a more robust alignment.
abstract: Human visual preferences are inherently multi-dimensional, encompassing aesthetics, detail fidelity, and semantic alignment. However, existing datasets provide only single, holistic annotations, resulting in severe label noise: images that excel in some dimensions but are deficient in others are simply marked as winner or loser. We theoretically demonstrate that compressing multi-dimensional preferences into binary labels generates conflicting gradient signals that misguide Diffusion Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). To address this, we propose Semi-DPO, a semi-supervised approach that treats consistent pairs as clean labeled data and conflicting ones as noisy unlabeled data. Our method starts by training on a consensus-filtered clean subset, then uses this model as an implicit classifier to generate pseudo-labels for the noisy set for iterative refinement. Experimental results demonstrate that Semi-DPO achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly improves alignment with complex human preferences, without requiring additional human annotation or explicit reward models during training. We will release our code and models at: https://github.com/L-CodingSpace/semi-dpo
